text: Feel your emotions, do not think about them. When we experience a negative emotion, a desire often comes to “sort it out” - that is, to understand what its cause is, what it is for, for what... It happens that indeed a single moment of such awareness is enough for the state to change to a blissful one. But more often it happens that this does not work, while the mind gets stuck in attempts to understand, and its long internal dialogue can pile up a whole garden even where there was none... So, try not to jump from anahata to ajna (each chakra must solve its own tasks), but to become aware of this emotion, to feel it and at the same time investigate it. Remaining in the body, perceive it as a pure bodily sensation - where exactly is it located? How does it feel - expansion or contraction, cold or heat, does it move in some direction?... Once it enters the zone of your attention, the emotion will begin to transform. Support the process of transformation with your breath (pranayama). Perhaps, in this flow, the body will push you into some asana... Continue the practice until you notice that there is no longer an object for your attention (the emotion has transformed). Acting in this way - fully immersed in feeling, you come out from under the power of the story that you yourself (that is, your mind) are winding around it.
